words.sense: Morally outrageous and deliberately wicked or criminal.
misconceptions: Confused with notorious when the defining clue is overlooked.
Confused with nefarious when the defining clue is overlooked.

semantic_axes.description: Nefarious describes the moral wickedness of an act; notorious describes how widely its bad reputation is known.

edges.boundary_rule: Nefarious describes the moral wickedness of an act; notorious describes how widely its bad reputation is known.
clues_a: Morally outrageous and deliberately wicked or criminal.
irrelevant_clues: format, colour, or popularity unless they establish the boundary
location or timing that does not change the decisive feature

misconceptions.M1: Treating nefarious as though it always means notorious.
misconceptions.M2: Treating notorious as though it always means nefarious.
misconceptions.M3: Overvaluing a distracting detail instead of the decisive semantic distinction.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Ana’s plan involving flood donations?

beats.text: Ana forged signatures so she could take relief payments meant for households whose homes had flooded.
beats.decisive_clue: she committed deliberate fraud against people awaiting aid
beats.reason: This establishes that she committed deliberate fraud against people awaiting aid.

beats.text: She directed the money to an account under her own control.
beats.decisive_clue: she committed deliberate fraud against people awaiting aid
beats.reason: Routing the funds to herself exposes the purpose of the fraud, not simply its reputation.

chains.feedback_short: She committed deliberate fraud against people awaiting aid; that detail favors nefarious.
chains.feedback_deep: Routing the funds to herself exposes the purpose of the fraud, not simply its reputation. Nefarious describes the moral wickedness of an act; notorious describes how widely its bad reputation is known.
chains.contrast_rule: Nefarious means wicked; notorious means badly known.

hints.attention: Judge what the scheme does to others.
hints.axis: Nefarious describes the moral wickedness of an act; notorious describes how widely its bad reputation is known.
hints.contrast: Nefarious means wicked; notorious means badly known.
